rows.query: How can I sign up for a new CareBridge account?
rows.answer: To sign up for a new CareBridge account, you can use the CareBridge app by registering with your email and password, or by using Google [FAQ-000001]. Please note that all new sign-ups are automatically created as patient accounts [FAQ-000001, FAQ-000007]. Additionally, each person must have their own individual account, as accounts cannot be shared [FAQ-000006].
rows.reason: The answer is fully supported by the provided passages and directly explains how to sign up for a new account.

rows.query: What are the steps to book a doctor appointment?
rows.answer: To book an appointment, open the "Book Appointment" section in the app [FAQ-000009]. Select a doctor, a date, and an available time slot [FAQ-000009]. You can view doctor specializations, fees, and working days in the doctor list to help you choose [FAQ-000011, FAQ-000056]. Only listed slots that are not already booked can be selected [FAQ-000012]. Finally, enter the reason for your visit to initiate the booking, which will begin with a "requested" status [FAQ-000009].
rows.reason: The answer accurately and comprehensively outlines the steps to book an appointment based entirely on the provided passages.

rows.query: What are the steps to book a doctor appointment?

Finally, enter a short reason for your visit [FAQ-000009, FAQ-000010]. Once these steps are completed, the booking status will be set to "requested" [FAQ-000009].
rows.reason: The answer accurately and completely outlines the steps to book an appointment based on the provided passages.

rows.query: What does it mean when my appointment says requested?
rows.answer: When your appointment status is "requested," it means that reception has not yet confirmed your booking [FAQ-000013]. Reception will confirm the appointment within the same working day [FAQ-000013]. You can still cancel your appointment while it is in this requested status [FAQ-000021, FAQ-000022]. Once confirmed, the status in "My Appointments" will update to "confirmed" [FAQ-000014].
rows.reason: The answer is fully supported by the provided passages and directly and comprehensively explains what the 'requested' status means.

rows.query: How do I cancel my booking?
rows.answer: To cancel your booking, open the "My Appointments" section and select the option to cancel [FAQ-000021]. You are only able to cancel appointments that have a status of "requested" or "confirmed" [FAQ-000021, FAQ-000022]. Completed appointments cannot be cancelled [FAQ-000022, FAQ-000026].
rows.reason: The answer is fully supported by the provided passages and directly explains how to cancel a booking, including the conditions under which it is allowed.

rows.query: Can I move my appointment to another day?
rows.answer: Yes, you can reschedule an appointment by opening "My Appointments" and selecting the reschedule option [FAQ-000024]. You must choose a new date in the future that corresponds to one of the doctor's available slots on a working day [FAQ-000024, FAQ-000025]. Please note that only requested or confirmed appointments are eligible for rescheduling [FAQ-000025]. Completed appointments cannot be rescheduled; you must book a new follow-up appointment instead [FAQ-000026].
rows.reason: The answer is fully supported by the provided passages and completely explains how and when the user can reschedule their appointment.

rows.query: How does the clinic waitlist work?
rows.answer: You can join the waitlist when your preferred slot or day with a doctor is full [FAQ-000030]. You are limited to one open waitlist entry per doctor and day [FAQ-000030]. When a slot becomes available, the next patient on the list receives an offer via a notification under the bell icon and in "My Appointments" [FAQ-000029, FAQ-000031]. You have 120 minutes to accept the offer in "My Appointments" [FAQ-000032]. If you do not accept within this timeframe, the offer expires and the slot is offered to the next patient on the waitlist [FAQ-000032, FAQ-000033]. You may join the waitlist again if your offer expires [FAQ-000033].
rows.reason: The answer is fully faithful to the provided passages and completely explains how the clinic waitlist works.

rows.query: I am very thirsty all the time and urinate a lot
rows.answer:
Feeling thirsty and urinating frequently are symptoms associated with Type 2 diabetes mellitus [VN-010041, VN-005122, VN-000228, VN-007880, VN-005781]. If you are experiencing these symptoms, you should consult a doctor for an evaluation, which may include tests such as fasting glucose and HbA1c [VN-010041, VN-005122, VN-000228, VN-007880, VN-005781]. 

General management advice provided to patients with these symptoms includes reducing rice portions and sweets, engaging in 30 minutes of brisk walking five days a week, checking fasting sugar twice weekly, and inspecting the feet daily [VN-010041, VN-005122, VN-000228, VN-007880, VN-005781]. Please schedule an appointment with a healthcare provider for a proper diagnosis and personalized treatment plan.
rows.reason: The answer is fully supported by the provided clinical notes and directly addresses the user's symptoms with relevant medical context and advice.

rows.query: Painful periods with bad cramps every month
rows.answer:
Patients experiencing painful cramps during the first days of their periods are often diagnosed with primary dysmenorrhoea [VN-002716, VN-004393, VN-004193, VN-001523]. Symptoms may include nausea and the severity of pain can lead to missed work or classes [VN-002716, VN-004393, VN-004193, VN-001523]. Stressful life events, such as family moves, have been reported to worsen these symptoms [VN-000338, VN-002716, VN-004393, VN-004193].

Recommended management strategies include using a hot water bottle, performing light exercise, and maintaining a period diary [VN-002716, VN-004393, VN-004193, VN-001523]. Medical providers may also issue prescriptions for pain management [VN-002716, VN-004393, VN-004193, VN-001523].
